summary:
Round 4 average is 75.3 (Milton 80, Neumann 74, Mensch 72). No record was tied to the wrong person and there were no privacy violations. Most of what is wrong comes from three shared causes, all checked in the code.

1. Role tenures are never recorded. addRoleAnchor (identity.js:245) is called only by restoreSubject. Every matchSubject call (finding.js:128, deepCheck.js:394) passes no date, and roleMatch returns null at identity.js:336 without one. So report.js afterTenure (line 337) never fires, and headlines that name only the role ("WeWork CEO gives back $5.9M") are never tied to the person.

2. Headline-only press about the subject is graded "possible" when it names the subject alongside a known event or counterparty. As a result, Milton's own S.D.N.Y. docket and pardon coverage appear under POSSIBLE NAMESAKES, and about 20 Neumann stories are matched by name only.

3. Readers stop at one passage or one language. sec.js personRelated keeps one bestSpot per filing (line 1206), which misses the WeWork loans (a MUST item). wpCompany reads only English Wikipedia, which misses Cédric O.

The other shared problems:
- **Severity and ordering:** NEGATED_PROBE (finding.js:162) has no "face" verb, does not accept the typographic apostrophe, and has no reject/decline form. So the UK competition regulator's clearance of Mistral is shown as a concern. redFlags.sort orders by record number only (report.js:401).
- **Dedupe:** pageKey includes the category and quoteKey includes the source (deepCheck.js:113-123).
- **Related parties:** report.js links a record to a related party only through data.person (line 448).
- **Coverage:** a state register that times out is not counted as a failure.

Dropped:
- The Wikidata-descriptor anchor (generic words like "AI" next to a name would tie namesakes to the subject).
- The surname-plus-company-anchor upgrade (a surname alone is a namesake risk).
- Any change that would upgrade to 'confirmed'.

The new anchors that are kept are capped at 'likely'. The pacing fix overlaps with work other engineers are already doing.

fixes.change:
Record role tenures and pass dates when grading.
(1) In the Wikidata roles reader (knowledge.js around rolesQuery/roleRows, ~line 652), on an entity already confirmed as the subject: for each row that is P169 (CEO of), a P39/P108 position whose label contains 'chief executive' or 'CEO', or P112 (founded by), call addRoleAnchor(subject, { org, role: 'ceo' or 'founder', from: pq:P580, to: pq:P582, origin: finding.id }).
(2) In sec.js, a Form D that lists the person as Executive Officer of an issuer already tied to them adds a role with a from-date only.
(3) Accept role 'founder' in roleMatch only when Wikidata P112 for that company lists exactly one person and that person is the subject. Then '<Company> founder' with no name, dated inside or after the tenure, grades 'likely'. The existing isOther/otherHolder guards still apply.
(4) Pass the record's date into grading: in makeFinding (finding.js:128) call matchSubject(subject, text, { date: f.date }). Store the date on the finding (e.g. gradeDate) so that gradeOf/regrade (deepCheck.js:393-401) also pass { date }. Today no caller passes a date, so roleMatch always returns null.
fixes.why: With no role anchors and no dates, three features are dead code: roleMatch, report.afterTenure and the tenures list. That is why 'WeWork CEO gives back $5.9M from We trademark' (#81) and 'landlord to WeWork' (#212) are not tied to Neumann, and why the AP and HN 'Nikola founder… pardon' stories are graded 'company'. It is also why bankruptcy and buy-back news from years after each person left is listed as their red flag (Neumann #1/#7/#12/#17, Milton #58).

fixes.change:
Widen NEGATED_PROBE (line 162):
(a) Replace won'?t with won['’]?t.
(b) Add 'face' and 'be subject to' to the verbs after won't, will not, would not and did not, for example (?:won['’]?t|will not|would not|did not)\s+(?:face|be subject to)\b${PROBE_GAP}\b${PROBE_WORD}.
(c) Add a reject/rule-out alternative: (?:reject(?:s|ed|ing)?|rul(?:es|ed|ing) out|dismiss(?:es|ed)?)\b${PROBE_GAP}\b${PROBE_WORD}.
Add unit tests for these two headlines, which must come out 'info': 'Microsoft partnership with France’s Mistral AI won’t face British antitrust probe' and 'UK's CMA rejects probe into Microsoft-Mistral AI tie-up'.
fixes.why: A regulator clearing the company is currently graded medium and shown as the only company concern in a clean subject's brief. A false concern costs investor trust and affects every subject with a 'probe cleared' headline.

fixes.change: In personRelated (~lines 1193-1215), for a main disclosure (S-1, F-1, 10-K, DEF 14A) from a registrant already tied to the person, collect up to 3 dealing passages instead of the single bestSpot(text, own, dealScore). Take the best spot from each DEAL_TERM family: (i) lease or landlord; (ii) loan, promissory note or line of credit; (iii) trademark, intellectual property or 'purchased from'. Discard any spot within 560 characters of one already chosen. Each passage becomes its own record with the filing's grade. Extra passages do not count against RELATED_MAX_READS (line 1161), which still caps how many documents are opened. Also raise the kin passage (kinOnlyScore) when the passage says 'other members of [his/her] family' even when no relative is named, but quote it without naming anyone who has no public role.
fixes.why: The We Co. S-1/A sets out the leases, the $5.9M 'We' trademark purchase and the loans to Neumann as separate paragraphs. Only the lease paragraph was kept, so the loans (a MUST item) are missing, and the trademark appears only through an HN story that is not tied to him.

fixes.change:
Add two anchor kinds. Both may raise a grade only to 'likely', never 'confirmed', and both still require the subject's full name in the text.
(1) 'events': when the check holds a confirmed regulator, court or Wikidata record of a conviction, sentence, pardon, indictment or charge, or an SEC complaint, register the event word family with the record's date. In matchSubject, a text with the full name plus that event word (convicted/found guilty, sentenced, pardoned, indicted/charged), dated on or after the event, grades 'likely' with the reason 'names <event> reported in <record n>'.
(2) 'encyclopedia': from the confirmed subject's own Wikipedia lead and career section and its LittleSis entry, add the linked organisations and people (investors, acquirers, co-founders, counterparties) as company/people anchors with origin 'encyclopedia'. They count like 'schools' anchors: full name plus one anchor gives 'likely'.
fixes.why: Headline-only stories that are plainly about the subject are listed as possible namesakes. Milton: FOX 13 and Park Record 'pardon of Utah billionaire Trevor Milton who was convicted of fraud' (#95/#96), and #119, #217, #219, #220. Neumann: 'Adam Neumann, SoftBank Near Settlement' (#65), and the NYT a16z, Semafor and TIME items (#255-#272). Mensch has a similar under-grading pattern with no event or counterparty in the headline ([108]-[122]); that case is left alone because a descriptor anchor would risk tying namesakes to him.

fixes.change:
(1) In storyFinding (lines 402-417), when a company is passed, do not hard-set match:'company'. Grade the story first with matchText = title + text and the story date. Use match:'company' only when that grade is 'none' or 'possible', so that a role or name match ('likely'/'confirmed') wins.
(2) In hnAboutCompany (~line 486), drop a company-only story dated before the year the person's tie to that company began (role anchor 'from', or the thread's earliest dated record).
(3) Drop a company-only story where a different capitalised organisation directly precedes a one-word company name used as a common noun ('Facebook Launches Flow').
fixes.why: #81 ($5.9M 'We' trademark) and #212 (Neumann 'makes millions as landlord to WeWork') are about him but were locked at company/info. #213 (Facebook's 2014 Flow type checker) was attributed to his 2022 company, Flow.

fixes.change:
Fix red-flag ordering and severity.
(a) Replace redFlags.sort((a,b)=>a.n-b.n) at line 401 with a sort by event weight, then source authority, then n. The weights, highest first: criminal (indict/convict/sentence); regulator action (SEC/DOJ/charged); lawsuit or settlement against the person; related-party or self-dealing; forced departure; everything else.
(b) In the afterTenure branch (line 394), drop the `tied !== list` condition, so a matter whose only adverse content is the insolvency of a company the person had already left moves to companyMatters even when the record names the person.
(c) Add to MEDIUM (line 153): 'landlord to', 'related[- ]party (?:transactions?|deals?)', 'self[- ]dealing', 'conflicts? of interest', 'bankrupt\b', 'chapter 11'.
(d) Treat 'steps down'/'stepped down' within 30 days of a role anchor's end date as the same departure matter, so the low-severity WSJ, CNBC and HN records join the medium-severity NYT 'under pressure' matter.
fixes.why: For Neumann, the top four red flags are a 2024 buy-back sentence, a refinancing quote and a proxy statement. The 2019 S-1 self-dealing ranks 5th and 6th and the forced step-down ranks 15th. 'WeWork Goes Bankrupt' is graded info. An investor reading top-down sees the least important items first.

Milton's own criminal docket (#66/#67) is listed under POSSIBLE NAMESAKES with high severity, and the case number 21-cr-478, a MUST item, never appears. Requiring the same district, a tight date window and a confirmed charge record keeps namesake risk negligible.

fixes.change:
Read related parties and backers in the company's home language.
(1) In wpCompany (knowledge.js ~line 840), after the en article, also fetch the company article on each language in languageHints(subject) (import it from ./web). Apply the same check that the title equals the company name. Run French role patterns on that article: CO_ROLE_FR = actionnaire|conseill(?:er|ère)(?:\s+en\s+[\wé ]+)?|administrat(?:eur|rice)|membre du conseil d'administration|investisseur|cofondat(?:eur|rice), with the shape `(${CO_PERSON})\s*,\s+(?:l['’]|le |la |un |une )?(?:ancien(?:ne)?\s+[^,]{0,40},?\s+)?(?:${CO_ROLE_FR})\b[^.]{0,60}?\bde\s+<company>`. Map each role to its English label.
(2) In associatesFromText (extract.js), add French equivalents of the co-founder, 'founded with' and '<Name>, shareholder/adviser' patterns. Run them only when languageHints includes 'fr' or the sentence contains French letters or function words.
(3) In web.js companyTemplates: raise q.company-backers prior from 0.35 to 0.5. Add q.company-investors: `"<c>" ("led by" OR "lead investor" OR "Series A" OR "Series B" OR "Series C")`. When languageHints has 'fr', add a French backers template: `"<c>" (actionnaire OR conseiller OR "ancien ministre" OR "conflit d'intérêts")`.
fixes.why: Cédric O, the former minister who advises Mistral and holds shares in it (its main conflict-of-interest question), is absent; he is named only on fr.wikipedia and in French press. ASML, the Series C lead, and all other investor names are also absent, so the cap table cannot be read.

fixes.change:
Attach records to related parties.
(1) In the related-party pass (report.js ~lines 448-451), also push a cited record to a party when any of these holds:
- personKey matches a name in f.data.relatives[], f.data.relatedPersons[] or f.data.persons[];
- the record is confirmed or likely for the subject and nameMatcher([party.name]) matches its title or quote (full name only).
(2) When party.role is null, fill it from relatedPersons[].roles, or from '<Name> (?:to assume|named|becomes) (?:the )?<Role>' / '<Role> <Name>' in a cited record.
(3) In deepCheck's duplicate branch (~line 624, seenIds/seenUrls hit), when task.kind is 'associate' or 'relative', append task.value to kept.data.persons before continuing.
fixes.why: All four of Milton's related parties show 0 records, although S-1 #110, #121/#128/#129 and the dHybrid Form D #130 name them. Mark Russell's role is null although #129 states he became CEO. Joint associate queries return pages already kept and are discarded without tagging the person.

fixes.change: In extractFounderEvidence's COMPANY_PATTERNS loop (the nearName(text, hasName, re) call before cleanCompany), reject a match when another person is named first. The test: the text directly before the role span matches /([A-ZÀ-Þ][\p{L}'’-]+\s+[A-ZÀ-Þ][\p{L}'’-]+),\s*(?:the\s+)?$/u and !hasName(that name). Equivalently, require that the nearest person name before the role word is the subject's.
fixes.why: 'Arthur Mensch, co-founder… of Mistral AI, and Guillaume Faury, CEO of Airbus' produced an 'Airbus' company thread for the subject (reproduced live). That wasted register lookups and lists Airbus as one of his companies. Any press release naming two executives triggers this.

fixes.change:
(1) For company threads that are prior ventures (dated in a Form D or Wikipedia career passage before the given company), add a template `"<Company>" "<Subject>" (sued OR lawsuit OR judgment)` with prefer:'reference' and allowMetered.
(2) In searchEngines.js, when the only engine available is the Google News RSS fallback and the lookup has prefer:'reference', do not let the fallback answer. Report the lookup as not run ('needs a general web search; news feed covers recent items only'), so the gap shows in coverage instead of returning recent coverage that is already known.
fixes.why: The Swift Transportation v. dHybrid suit (a SHOULD item) was unreachable because DuckDuckGo was paused and the fallback is a recency-biased news feed. Any older lawsuit about an earlier venture is lost in the same way, and silently.

fixes.change:
Report partial and blocked failures honestly.
(1) In the state-register loop (registries.js ~lines 997-1011), collect the states that timed out and return them on the result (result.partial = ['Colorado', ...]) instead of adding only a note.
(2) In deepCheck's stat accounting (~line 604), add stat.partial. Have report.coverage.partlyAnswered list 'US state business registers: Colorado, New York, Texas did not answer in time', and remove those states from the searched label.
(3) In the deepCheck catch block, store a sanitized failure class (HTTP status, timeout, DNS/TLS, blocked by host) next to plainFailure's text and write it to the run log.
(4) In archive.js, detect the Wayback 'suspected abusive bot traffic' page and report it as 'turned automated requests away', not as a timeout.
fixes.why: Coverage shows 0 failures for state registers while four states timed out, which overstates what was searched. News-archive and Wayback failures cannot be diagnosed, and some 'timeouts' are actually bot blocks.

fixes.change: Pacing (check first whether the pacing work already covers this). When the queue holds only lookups waiting for a resting search host, and no lookup is running, drop the waiting lookups after tailWaitMs, or at once when their prior is below 0.45, instead of waiting for maxWaitAgeMs (12 min). Record them in coverage as not run.
fixes.why: The Mensch run sat idle from about 360s to 720s for 2 web lookups that were then dropped anyway. The Milton run idled about 100s with 6 queued and nothing running. That doubles runtime for 0 records.

fixes.change: In quotedDeepBrief, under '## RED FLAGS', add a 'Screens with no match:' line listing the screens that came back clean. Build it from report.coverage.searched entries with records===0, failed===0 and an id in a SCREEN set: sanctions-lists, us-exclusions, wanted-lists, finra-brokercheck, court-records-open, uk-case-law, doj-press-releases, us-enforcement-actions, uk-gazette, bodacc, icij. Use their human labels, for example 'sanctions (US, UN, EU, UK, Canada), US exclusion lists, FBI/EU wanted lists, FINRA, DOJ releases, ICIJ'. Show the line even when there are red flags.
fixes.why: Clean screens appear only in log[]. 'None found in the records searched' does not tell an investor which screens ran, which is the main reassurance for a clean subject.

fixes.change:
Merge duplicate records.
(1) pageKey (line 113): drop f.category for non-archive records, keying on `${urlKey(f.url)}|${headline(f.title)}`. For wikipedia.org/wiki/<Title> URLs, key on the normalised URL alone (fragment stripped), so a web-search copy of an article the wikipedia source already holds is dropped.
(2) quoteKey (line 119): replace f.source with a source family (the prefix before the first '-', so sec-filings and sec-company are both 'sec'), so the CoreWeave quote in [6] merges into [5].
(3) Add taid to TRACKING (line 142), and strip a leading 'Hacker News (N points…): ' prefix in headline().
(4) Let upgradeKept apply to archive summary records of the same page. Normalise country subdomains (fr.linkedin.com to linkedin.com) in urlKey for profile hosts, so a copy reached from a Wikidata link lifts the copy whose address was guessed from the name and replaces it.
fixes.why: There are duplicate pairs in every report: Wikipedia #11/#56 (#56 quoting reference-list text, listed as a high red flag), [10]/[57] across sections, [5]/[6], the Economist interview [41]/[110] graded differently, LinkedIn [12]/[89], and HN copies of press stories. They inflate counts and repeat red flags.

fixes.change:
Fix event dates.
(1) For Wikipedia passage records, take the date from the first year named in the passage's first sentence (the sentence used as its title), not from the latest year in the whole quotation (helper ~line 706).
(2) For Google News RSS items, mark the date approximate (data.dateApprox) when the URL slug or headline names a year earlier than the RSS date, or when the headline says 'CEO <name>' in the present tense after the role anchor's end. Keep approximate-dated records off the timeline and out of recency ranking.
(3) Flag a Wikidata role start date that is earlier than the company's founding date in the report (WeWork CEO from 2008-05, founded 2010) as an inconsistency instead of listing it as a timeline event.
fixes.why: Milton's 2020 resignation and 2021 indictment are dated 2024-09 and appear after his sentencing. A 2019 ABC story about Neumann is dated 2026-02-14. Neumann's CEO start date predates the company.

fixes.change: Apply the CIK/registrant tie that personRelated uses (cikTie/gradeByTie) to the plain full-text 'mentions' path (~line 1752). An accession already tied to the person's company grades the same as the related-party record, and is merged into it when the accession matches. For counterparty filers, run gradeByTie with the company anchors against the passage that was read, so a filing that names the subject and his company grades 'company' or 'likely'.
fixes.why: #225/#226 come from the same We Co. S-1/A accession as confirmed #6 but are graded possible. The GM 8-K (#207) and CNH 6-K (#208) documenting Nikola's partnerships, and the Selina filings naming Neumann's family office, are listed as name-only matches.

fixes.change: When threads are extracted from confirmed press records and Wikipedia career passages, read the snippet or quote as well as the title. Add patterns for earlier ventures: 'startups? (?:called|named) (NAME)', 'founded (NAME)', 'an? (?:online )?(?:marketplace|company|startup),\s+(NAME)'. Accept a name only if it is capitalised and is not the given company or a known publisher.
fixes.why: uPillar (a SHOULD item) is never extracted, although the WSJ #170 and BI #168 pieces that cover it are already in the report. Earlier failed ventures matter to an investor.

fixes.change:
(1) Add the given company's own domain (from Wikidata P856 or a confirmed company record) /about, /team and /leadership pages to the candidate URLs, and compare the earliest and latest readable snapshots for claims about the subject.
(2) In bioText, cut at the first /\b(see more|voir plus|ver más|mehr anzeigen)\b/i and drop sentences matching /Welcome back|Email or phone|Forgot password|Te damos la bienvenida|Contraseña|User Agreement|Condiciones de uso/i.
(3) For LinkedIn JSON-LD roles where startDate===endDate on a past role, drop the dates so compareClaims does not diff them.
(4) When a profile has more than one capture, read the earliest and latest instead of only one (e.g. the Twitter 2019 and 2023+ bios).
fixes.why: The company's own pages, where the most disputed founder claims changed, are never compared over time. LinkedIn quotes carry login-page text. The JSON-LD dates ('DeepMind 2023-05 - 2023-05') could produce a false 'dates changed' finding.

fixes.change: In wikipediaKind (line 326), classify a Wikipedia title equal to the subject's surname or first name alone ('Neumann', 'Trevor') as 'list'. Cap Wikipedia articles of kind 'other' at 3 per check, and file them under a 'Background' group instead of Press.
fixes.why: About 15 unrelated Wikipedia pages (Bill Graham, Andrew Ross Sorkin, the 'Neumann' surname list, 'Trevor - Wikipedia', '2021 in the United States') add clutter to the press section.

fixes.change: Run the French company register and BODACC tasks only when France is linked to the subject: the company's LEI country, Wikidata P17/P159 country or register hit is FR, languageHints(subject) includes 'fr', or a confirmed record places the subject in France. Apply the same rule to other national registers through a country map.
fixes.why: Seven lookups, two of them timeouts, were spent on French registers for a US company, which adds to the pacing pressure.

fixes.change: When quoting a relative's blurb, strip clauses that only describe a family tie to a third party: /\b(?:cousin|niece|nephew|aunt|uncle|sister|brother|daughter|son)(?:-in-law)? of [^.;,]+[.;,]?/i. Keep the relative's own business or public role.
fixes.why: #112 quotes a relative's celebrity-cousin tie, which is unrelated to any business role. The change tightens the privacy rule at no cost to diligence.

grades.subject: Trevor Milton / Nikola (round 4, r5 run: 229 records, 5 rounds, 157 lookups, 277s)
grades.recallMust: 8 of 9 MUST facts are found and tied to him as confirmed. Found: conviction in Oct 2022 in S.D.N.Y. (Wikidata #5/#6, Wikipedia #2, CBS/CNN/CNBC #33-#40, FreightWaves #80); four-year sentence in Dec 2023 (DOJ press release #3, notice to victims #4, Reuters/BBC/CNN #18-#27); presidential pardon in March 2025 (CNBC #14, KJZZ #17, HN #13/#15, Wikipedia #60); SEC charges in July 2021 (SEC complaint #8 No. 1:21-cv-06445, SEC release 2021-141 #59, DOJ charge release #9); Nikola's $125M settlement in Dec 2021 (SEC release 2021-267 #7, Axios #83); the Hindenburg report in Sept 2020 (Wikipedia #10, dated 2020-09-10); resignation as executive chairman in Sept 2020 (WSJ #85, NBC #86, Forbes #88, 8-K #97). MISS: the criminal case number US v. Milton, 21-cr-478 appears nowhere. The two S.D.N.Y. "United States v. Milton" dockets (#66, #67) were found but graded possible, with caseNumber null, and filed under POSSIBLE NAMESAKES. An investor therefore sees the subject's own criminal docket listed as a possible namesake's case.
grades.recallShould: 5 of 7. Found: dHybrid (Form D #130 lists Trevor Robert Milton as Executive Officer and Director of dHybrid, Inc. in 2011; Wikipedia #118 and #134; Crunchbase archive #188/#189). St. George Security and Alarm (Wikipedia #134 quote only; a thread was opened but it produced no record of its own). Arbitration award to Nikola (FreightWaves #79 "claws back $165 million"; Wikipedia #1 gives about $168M confirmed in Sept 2024). Nikola Chapter 11 in Feb 2025 (Wikipedia #58; CNBC/Guardian/Reuters #101-#103 as company records). Left Utah Valley University without a degree (Wikipedia #132 "dropped out after one semester"; Wikidata #131). MISSES: (1) Swift Transportation's lawsuit against dHybrid. The dHybrid thread was pulled, but the keyless web search fell back to Google News RSS because DuckDuckGo was paused. A live probe of the q.company-legal query '"dHybrid" (lawsuit OR fraud OR investigation)' returned only recent Nikola coverage that was already in the report (BI #167/#168, FT #169). The 2013-era suit is not reachable through a recency-biased news engine, and the federal-docket title archive does not cover state courts. (2) uPillar: never extracted as a thread, and no record names it. The WSJ "Long Before Nikola Trucks, Trevor Milton Sold Investors on Startups That Faded" (#170) and BI "Tumultuous Past" (#168) cover it, but only their headlines are kept.
grades.noise: 1) Under-grading of plainly-his records puts them in POSSIBLE NAMESAKES and "matched by name only": #95 FOX 13 "Trump explains pardon of Utah billionaire Trevor Milton who was convicted of fraud", #96 Park Record "Trump pardons convicted former Summit County resident Trevor Milton", #119 TokenPost (FBI account), #217 The Information, #219 The Hill "Who is Trevor Milton, the startup founder and donor pardoned by Trump", #220 FreightWaves "Trevor Milton trial delayed". The S.D.N.Y. criminal dockets #66/#67 are listed as possible namesakes with high severity. A live probe confirmed that matchSubject returns possible for the FOX 13 headline, and none for AP #61 "Convicted of bilking investors, Nikola founder and Trump donor gets a presidential pardon", which ends up graded "company". The same applies to HN #63/#106 ("Nikola founder…"). EDGAR hits by counterparties are possible only: GM 8-K #207 (the Sept 2020 partnership), CNH 6-K #208. 2) Duplicates: Wikipedia appears as #11 (Wikipedia source, identity) and again as #56 (web-search, press, high red flag) for the same URL. #56's quote is reference-list junk ("Retrieved November 6, 2026"). pageKey includes category and headline, so the two are not merged. Red flags #1, #2, #11, #56 and #60 are all the same Wikipedia article. 36 red flags carry many repeats of the same events: ten sentencing articles, eight conviction articles. 3) Generic pages: #225 "Trevor - Wikipedia", #228 History of GM, #229 "2021 in the United States", graded possible/info, which is harmless but clutter. 4) Timeline/dating: Wikipedia passage #1 ("In 2020, Milton resigned…") and #2 ("In July 2021… indictment") are dated 2024-09 because knowledge.js dates a passage by the latest year it names. On the timeline they sit after the 2023 sentencing. #134 career passage is dated 2015. 5) Severity: #58 (Nikola Chapter 11) is counted as a person red flag rather than a company matter, which is minor. Otherwise the top red flags (DOJ sentencing, Wikidata convictions, SEC $125M, SEC complaint, DOJ charges, Hindenburg) are the right ones, in a sensible order. 6) Wasted lookups: the French company register (5 lookups, 2 timeouts) and BODACC were searched for a US company.
sourcesFailing: Web archive (earlier versions of profiles and bios): 3 of 8 lookups failed, 'could not be reached'. Reported in coverage, and trevormilton.com was 'not answered by the archive'.
Patents (Google Patents): 'could not be reached'. Listed under NOT SEARCHED (honest). Nikola/Milton design patents, e.g. the Tesla Semi design dispute, were therefore not checked.
French company register (Annuaire des Entreprises): 2 of 5 lookups 'did not respond in time'. It should not have been queried for a US subject at all.

CourtListener: not enabled on this deployment (reported honestly). As a result, the S.D.N.Y. criminal case number 21-cr-478 is never shown. The Internet Archive copies (gov.uscourts.nysd.564174/564175) have no docket number in their metadata, only a CourtListener source_url.

Open-web search: DuckDuckGo paused ('asked for fewer searches'). The keyless fallback is Google News RSS, which is recency-biased, so the dHybrid company-legal lookup could not reach the older Swift Transportation lawsuit (confirmed with one live run).
Pacing: the round-3 status line repeats unchanged from 103s to 205s with 'queued 6' and nothing running, about 100s idle. Other engineers are already fixing pacing; noted, not proposed again.

grades.subject: Adam Neumann / WeWork (evaluation round 4, r5 run: 287 records, 178 confirmed, 16 red flags, 720s)
grades.recallMust: About 5.5 of the 7 MUST sub-facts are found and tied to him. FOUND: (1) Sept 2019 step-down: #36 NYT "Steps Down Under Pressure" (red flag), #37 CBS, #60 WSJ, #61/#38 HN, #63 Wikipedia "On September 24, 2019, he resigned", all confirmed. (2) Related-party leases in the S-1: #6 S-1/A We Co. 2019-09-13 (leases with landlord entities in which Adam has an ownership interest) and #5 S-1 2022 (landlord), both confirmed and medium red flags. (3) SoftBank $3B tender suit 2020: #25 NYT, #26 CNN, #28 Bloomberg, #29 CNBC "failed tender offer", #30 WSJ, #4 DEF 14A. (4) 2021 settlement: #21 Forbes, #22-24 WSJ/Fox, #3 Wikipedia. (5) Chapter 11 Nov 2023: #41 bankruptcy docket (company), #208 HN "WeWork Goes Bankrupt" (company), and confirmed press #19 and #20. PARTIAL: the $5.9M "We" trademark, given back, appears only as #81, an HN story graded company/low ("WeWork CEO gives back $5.9M from 'We' trademark"). It is not tied to him, not a red flag and not in the brief. A WSJ story on the same theme, #212 "WeWork's CEO Makes Millions as Landlord to WeWork", is also graded company/info. MISSED: company loans to Neumann. No record mentions a loan. The SEC related-party reader reads only one best passage per filing (sec.js personRelated: bestSpot), so the lease passage of the We Co. S-1/A is kept and the loan and trademark passages in the same document are never quoted. Its own note admits that 9 more related-party filings were not read.
